correctness.rationale: Campbell Lemmas 3, 4 and 6 have the needed hypotheses: arbitrarily large odd d with a size-(r+3) product-minimizer, existence of three distinct primes for all sufficiently large odd d, and complement optimality for prime p>d with strict next gap >11M. Both deletion sets lie in the prefix, and unique factorization makes the product optimizer unique. Fixed H excludes only O_H(y/log^2 y) primes by summing the unconditional two-linear-form upper-bound sieve (the two roots are distinct modulo every prime not dividing h for each fixed even shift h; odd shifts give only finite exceptions). A cross-prefix collision would force p''<=max|d_i-d_j|, already excluded by p''>max d_i; same-prefix collisions are impossible. Partial summation gives Sigma(y)~y^2/(2 log y), so with at most one boundary prime per translate the count is (2J+o(1))sqrt(X/log X). For every arbitrarily large fixed J this bounds the normalized liminf below by 2J, proving divergence without any growing-J uniformity. The frozen verification notes are analytic, not a computational certificate; its no-rate qualification is not a theorem about how slowly the actual count grows.
